rationale: Verified canonical oracle targets define target-likelihood supervision for every TRAIN row without requiring mixed sampled rewards; actual finite/nonzero/constrained gradients still require qualification.
An ascending-index teacher is the smallest positive-supervision acquisition baseline and avoids adding a teacher-order comparison before establishing R acquisition.
Equal-row completion-plus-EOS CE and one fixed pass over 3000 R TRAIN rows make the dose explicit; prompt and padding positions contribute zero.
One arm and one proposed seed limit this study to a feasibility baseline, with no seed-population, teacher-order, whole-skill composition or general no-forgetting claim.
